investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocks Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: The remote-agent-create eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: all 6 nodes were unavailable due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. As a direct consequence, the pod never reached a running state, no VM was assigned, and the eval produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, the agent pod remains in Pending/Unschedulable state for the full probe window (136 s for remote-agent-create, 126 s for remote-agent-runtime). Because the pod never starts, no VM ID is assigned and no remoteState is reachable, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime shares the identical scheduling failure message ('0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), confirming the constraint is cluster-wide and not specific to a single probe invocation.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256-259): requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod did not start.

sibling.remote-agent-state: GET /api/agents/[REDACTED]/remote_agent/state returned 502 with swarm gateway 500 and 'internal error: authentication service error', indicating a second independent failure path in the swarm layer that would block state retrieval even if scheduling recovered.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote', meaning the agent creation API call is the first step that triggers pod scheduling — a scheduling failure at this step prevents all downstream evidence collection.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or insufficient node pool size: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the effective schedulable pool is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, any new remote agent pod will be unschedulable regardless of overall cluster size.

TERTIARY — Swarm authentication service error (independent failure): sibling.remote-agent-state shows the swarm gateway returning 'internal error: authentication service error' (502/500). This is a distinct failure from the scheduling issue and would block state polling even after a pod is scheduled.

SPECULATIVE — Leaked or zombie remote agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up agent pods, VM slots may be held by idle workloads. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to prevent this, but cleanup failures in prior runs could leave orphaned pods.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and an alternative cause (e.g., a quota policy change or a node label change) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the probe immediately succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod is found to have changed such that 0 nodes match (not just 4 mismatching), the root cause would shift from VM slot exhaustion to a misconfigured or missing node label.

If the swarm authentication service error (sibling.remote-agent-state) is resolved independently and remote-agent-create still fails, it confirms the scheduling issue is the primary blocker rather than an auth dependency.
If orphaned pods from prior eval runs are found and removed, and the probe then succeeds, leaked pod cleanup would be the root cause rather than genuine cluster capacity exhaustion.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity/selector and that each has non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity, providing early warning before full exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agent State Eval Failure: Swarm Gateway 502 via Authentication Service Error + Kata PeerPods VM Exhaustion
investigation.summary: The remote-agent-state eval failed because GET /api/agents/[REDACTED]/remote_agent/state returned a 502 bad_gateway wrapping a swarm-internal 500 with error code "internal_error" and message "internal error: authentication service error" (evidence: failed-check.message). All four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing because the HTTP call never succeeded, so the runner could not populate any evidence (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence, failed-check.evidence). Both sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime independently failed with Kubernetes Unschedulable events citing exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across all 6 nodes (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime), indicating the swarm VM pool was saturated at the time of the run.
investigation.rootCause: The proximate cause of the remote-agent-state eval failure is a 502 response from the production API gateway, which itself received a 500 from the swarm backend carrying an "authentication service error" (evidence: failed-check.message). The broader infrastructure context is that the Kubernetes cluster running kata.peerpods.io peer-pod VMs was fully exhausted — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector — preventing both remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime from scheduling new pods (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime). Whether the authentication service error is a direct consequence of VM exhaustion (e.g., an auth sidecar or token-exchange service running inside a peer-pod that could not be scheduled) or an independent failure in the swarm authentication layer is uncertain without additional swarm-side logs. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: Runner calls createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId) before polling state, meaning agent creation failure upstream would prevent state polling from ever reaching a valid agent.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: Contract at line 264 requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state]; none were written because the HTTP response was an error.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm authentication service failure: The swarm backend returned error code 'internal_error' with message 'internal error: authentication service error', indicating the swarm's internal auth layer (token exchange, credential validation, or auth sidecar) was unavailable or erroring at the time of the eval run (evidence: failed-check.message).

CONTRIBUTING — Kata PeerPods VM pool exhaustion: All 6 Kubernetes nodes were unable to schedule new peer-pod VMs (2 with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 with affinity mismatch), which prevented remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime from provisioning VMs (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime). If the swarm auth service itself runs inside a peer-pod, pool exhaustion could be the root trigger for the auth error.

SECONDARY — Auth service dependency on peer-pod scheduling: If the swarm authentication service requires a freshly scheduled peer-pod VM to issue or validate tokens, VM pool exhaustion would cascade into auth failures, explaining why the state endpoint returned an auth error rather than a scheduling error.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Transient swarm gateway instability: The 502 bad_gateway wrapping a 500 could reflect a transient swarm gateway issue unrelated to VM scheduling, but the simultaneous failure of all three remote-agent checks makes a shared infrastructure cause more likely.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Runtime Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: The remote-agent-runtime eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: all 6 nodes were unavailable due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. The pod remained unscheduled for 126 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing all 5 required contract fields.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity to schedule a new agent pod. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, 2 that match the pod's node affinity/selector have exhausted their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable quota, and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never produces an agent, the probe exits with the scheduler error message, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has no remaining VM slots to schedule a new peer-pod, causing immediate Unschedulable status with no preemption path. Supported by both remote-agent-runtime (failed-check.message) and remote-agent-create (sibling.remote-agent-create) showing the identical scheduler rejection.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling domain to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. This is a configuration constraint that amplifies the capacity problem.

Tertiary — swarm authentication service degradation: sibling.remote-agent-state shows the swarm gateway returning a 500 internal_error / authentication service error. If the swarm control plane was also unhealthy, even a successfully scheduled pod might have failed to reach a ready state, but this is a downstream concern — the primary blocker is the scheduler rejection before any pod starts.

Lower confidence — transient cluster load spike: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads could temporarily exhaust kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The absence of run history (previousRunCount=0) means it is unknown whether this is a persistent or intermittent condition.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocks Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-create eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: all 6 nodes were unavailable due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. As a direct consequence, the pod never reached a running state, no VM was assigned, and the eval produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, the agent pod remains in Pending/Unschedulable state for the full probe window (136 s for remote-agent-create, 126 s for remote-agent-runtime). Because the pod never starts, no VM ID is assigned and no remoteState is reachable, causing a total contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime shares the identical scheduling failure message ('0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), confirming the constraint is cluster-wide and not specific to a single probe invocation.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141507, endedAt=2026-07-03T00:04:36.266Z — the probe ran for ~141 s before failing, well within the outageLatencyMs threshold of 360000 ms defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:183.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256-259): requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod did not start.

sibling.remote-agent-state: GET /api/agents/[REDACTED]/remote_agent/state returned 502 with swarm gateway 500 and 'internal error: authentication service error', indicating a second independent failure path in the swarm layer that would block state retrieval even if scheduling recovered.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote', meaning the agent creation API call is the first step that triggers pod scheduling — a scheduling failure at this step prevents all downstream evidence collection.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or insufficient node pool size: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the effective schedulable pool is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, any new remote agent pod will be unschedulable regardless of overall cluster size.

TERTIARY — Swarm authentication service error (independent failure): sibling.remote-agent-state shows the swarm gateway returning 'internal error: authentication service error' (502/500). This is a distinct failure from the scheduling issue and would block state polling even after a pod is scheduled.

SPECULATIVE — Leaked or zombie remote agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not clean up agent pods, VM slots may be held by idle workloads. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is intended to prevent this, but cleanup failures in prior runs could leave orphaned pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent State Eval Failure: Swarm Gateway 502 via Authentication Service Error + Kata PeerPods VM Exhaustion
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-state eval failed because GET /api/agents/[REDACTED]/remote_agent/state returned a 502 bad_gateway wrapping a swarm-internal 500 with error code "internal_error" and message "internal error: authentication service error" (evidence: failed-check.message). All four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing because the HTTP call never succeeded, so the runner could not populate any evidence (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence, failed-check.evidence). Both sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime independently failed with Kubernetes Unschedulable events citing exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across all 6 nodes (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime), indicating the swarm VM pool was saturated at the time of the run.
investigations.rootCause: The proximate cause of the remote-agent-state eval failure is a 502 response from the production API gateway, which itself received a 500 from the swarm backend carrying an "authentication service error" (evidence: failed-check.message). The broader infrastructure context is that the Kubernetes cluster running kata.peerpods.io peer-pod VMs was fully exhausted — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector — preventing both remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime from scheduling new pods (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime). Whether the authentication service error is a direct consequence of VM exhaustion (e.g., an auth sidecar or token-exchange service running inside a peer-pod that could not be scheduled) or an independent failure in the swarm authentication layer is uncertain without additional swarm-side logs. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: pod stuck unscheduled for 126s — same Unschedulable reason across all 6 nodes.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=108615, indicating the eval runner waited over 108 seconds before receiving the 502, consistent with a timeout or retry cycle against an unavailable backend.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: Runner calls createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId) before polling state, meaning agent creation failure upstream would prevent state polling from ever reaching a valid agent.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: Contract at line 264 requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state]; none were written because the HTTP response was an error.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm authentication service failure: The swarm backend returned error code 'internal_error' with message 'internal error: authentication service error', indicating the swarm's internal auth layer (token exchange, credential validation, or auth sidecar) was unavailable or erroring at the time of the eval run (evidence: failed-check.message).

CONTRIBUTING — Kata PeerPods VM pool exhaustion: All 6 Kubernetes nodes were unable to schedule new peer-pod VMs (2 with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 with affinity mismatch), which prevented remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime from provisioning VMs (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime). If the swarm auth service itself runs inside a peer-pod, pool exhaustion could be the root trigger for the auth error.

SECONDARY — Auth service dependency on peer-pod scheduling: If the swarm authentication service requires a freshly scheduled peer-pod VM to issue or validate tokens, VM pool exhaustion would cascade into auth failures, explaining why the state endpoint returned an auth error rather than a scheduling error.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Transient swarm gateway instability: The 502 bad_gateway wrapping a 500 could reflect a transient swarm gateway issue unrelated to VM scheduling, but the simultaneous failure of all three remote-agent checks makes a shared infrastructure cause more likely.

Extend the remote-agent-state eval to capture and surface the raw HTTP status code and error body as evidence fields (e.g., httpStatus, errorCode, errorMessage) so future failures include structured diagnostic data even when the contract evidence fields cannot be populated.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Runtime Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: The remote-agent-runtime eval failed because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: all 6 nodes were unavailable due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. The pod remained unscheduled for 126 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing all 5 required contract fields.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity to schedule a new agent pod. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, 2 that match the pod's node affinity/selector have exhausted their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable quota, and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never produces an agent, the probe exits with the scheduler error message, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 126s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, pod stuck for 136s, confirming the scheduling failure is reproducible across independent agent creation attempts in the same run window.

sibling.remote-agent-state: GET /api/agents/[REDACTED]/remote_agent/state returned 502 with swarm gateway 500 internal_error / authentication service error, indicating the swarm control plane was also degraded during the same window.
failed-check.evidence: empty object — zero evidence keys collected, consistent with the probe never reaching the agent runtime step.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the probe aborted before any runtime interaction.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=130091, which is well below the outageLatencyMs threshold of 420000 (source.check-config.remote-agent-runtime), so the failure is a hard scheduler error, not a latency breach.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: the runner calls createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) at line 1918 immediately after acquiring orgId; a scheduler failure at this step would prevent all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false, so this failure contributes to feature degradation scoring but does not by itself constitute a required-check outage.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has no remaining VM slots to schedule a new peer-pod, causing immediate Unschedulable status with no preemption path. Supported by both remote-agent-runtime (failed-check.message) and remote-agent-create (sibling.remote-agent-create) showing the identical scheduler rejection.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the effective scheduling domain to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. This is a configuration constraint that amplifies the capacity problem.

Tertiary — swarm authentication service degradation: sibling.remote-agent-state shows the swarm gateway returning a 500 internal_error / authentication service error. If the swarm control plane was also unhealthy, even a successfully scheduled pod might have failed to reach a ready state, but this is a downstream concern — the primary blocker is the scheduler rejection before any pod starts.

Lower confidence — transient cluster load spike: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads could temporarily exhaust kata.peerpods.io/vm slots. The absence of run history (previousRunCount=0) means it is unknown whether this is a persistent or intermittent condition.

reproductionSteps.details: remote-agent-create produced the same Unschedulable message (sibling.remote-agent-create); re-running it independently confirms whether the capacity constraint persists.

reproductionSteps.label: Run the remote-agent-state sibling probe to assess swarm gateway health independently
reproductionSteps.details: sibling.remote-agent-state showed a 502/500 authentication service error; re-running isolates whether the swarm control plane has recovered separately from the scheduler issue.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect Kubernetes node allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Query the cluster to see current allocatable and used kata.peerpods.io/vm counts on the nodes that match the pod's affinity selector, to confirm exhaustion and determine headroom.

affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes as the direct cause of the Unschedulable status (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to the 2 already-exhausted nodes (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Swarm gateway / authentication service
affectedAreas.reason: sibling.remote-agent-state shows the swarm gateway returning 500 internal_error with an authentication service error during the same run window, indicating a concurrent swarm control plane issue.

affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed in this run (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189). The feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, so two required-check failures (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) meet the outage threshold.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; a scheduler failure at this step prevents all subsequent evidence collection (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

recommendedNextActions: Investigate kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible Kubernetes nodes to determine whether the resource pool is fully consumed and whether any running peer-pods can be terminated to free capacity.

Review the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec to understand why 4 of 6 nodes are excluded; if the selector is overly restrictive, expanding it to additional nodes would increase the schedulable pool and reduce the risk of exhaustion.

Investigate the swarm gateway authentication service error surfaced by sibling.remote-agent-state (502 / internal_error / authentication service error) as a separate but concurrent degradation; determine if it shares a root cause with the scheduler issue (e.g., a shared VM or node pool).

Check whether any long-running or leaked remote agent pods are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that should have been released; the eval runner uses withCleanup (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1916), but prior failed runs may have left orphaned pods if cleanup did not execute.
Establish a run history baseline for the remote-agents checks (previousRunCount=0 in verifier history) so future regressions can be detected against a known-passing state.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval to check if scheduler failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was a transient spike. A pass would produce all 5 required evidence fields; a fail with the same message confirms persistence.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-create eval to independently confirm kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: sibling.remote-agent-create showed the identical scheduler message; re-running confirms whether the capacity constraint affects all new remote agent pod creation attempts.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-state eval to assess swarm gateway / authentication service recovery
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: sibling.remote-agent-state showed a 502/500 authentication service error; re-running determines if the swarm control plane has recovered independently of the scheduler issue.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to assess overall feature health
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Provides a combined view of the feature's current state and whether the degradedAfterFailures=1 / outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds are still being breached (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated eval source paths for any recent changes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: infra/evals/status/features.json, infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, and infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs all have recent-change.* entries; reviewing their current state confirms the eval contracts and runner logic are intact and the failure is infrastructure-side.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime succeeds and produces a scheduled pod, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion was transient and has since resolved.

If kubectl or cluster metrics show kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero on the affinity-eligible nodes, the scheduler message may reflect a race condition or stale resource accounting rather than true exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec was recently changed to target only the 2 nodes (rather than all 6), the scheduling domain reduction would be a configuration regression rather than a capacity problem — this would be shown by a diff of the pod spec or Helm values.
If remote-agent-state passes on re-run (no 502/authentication error), the swarm gateway degradation was independent and transient, not a contributing factor to the runtime eval failure.

If no-history context (previousRunCount=0) is due to a new eval environment rather than a first-ever failure, a passing run in a different environment would indicate the issue is environment-specific.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all affinity-eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, so scheduler exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure capacity signal rather than a timeout inside the agent creation probe.

Add a dedicated swarm gateway health eval that probes the authentication service endpoint directly, decoupled from the agent lifecycle checks, so authentication service errors are caught independently of pod scheduling failures.
Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the remote agent pod's node selector matches at least N nodes in the cluster, alerting when the schedulable pool drops below a safe threshold.

Once a passing run is established, configure the remote-agents feature history to retain at least 5 previous run statuses so currentlyRegressedFromPass can be computed and regressions are flagged automatically.
